title: QatarEnergy announces/resumes LNG production in Qatar by April 30?
description:
QatarEnergy, a Qatari state-owned petroleum company, announced on March 2 that it would halt production of liquefied natural gas (LNG) due to military strikes on its operating facilities (see: https://www.qatarenergy.qa/en/MediaCenter/Pages/newsdetails.aspx?ItemId=3892).

This market will resolve to “Yes” if QatarEnergy resumes production of liquefied natural gas at QatarEnergy LNG production facilities in Qatar, or officially announces that such production has resumed or will resume, by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

QatarEnergy resuming the production of other halted products, including downstream LNG-related products, or resuming transportation of LNG without resuming production, will not alone count.

An official announcement that LNG production will resume at QatarEnergy LNG production facilities in Qatar must signal the end of the total LNG production halt effective immediately or on a specific date or clearly defined time window. Mere statements that production will resume at some undefined point in the future, or that production will resume once the halt has ended, will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from QatarEnergy (https://www.qatarenergy.qa/en/Pages/vHome.aspx); however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Following a US-brokered ceasefire in the Middle East conflict, QatarEnergy mobilized engineers and workers in early April 2026 to restart liquefied natural gas production at its Ras Laffan facilities, shuttered since early March attacks that prompted force majeure declarations. Reuters and Bloomberg reports confirmed preparations underway, with two of three damaged trains reportedly back online amid reopening of Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes, restoring confidence in an announcement or resumption by April 30 deadline. Trader consensus at 99.8% Yes reflects this rapid progress from the world's top LNG exporter, though full capacity ramp-up may take months. Realistic shifts remain possible via official clarification of no verified production, resolution disputes, or renewed hostilities delaying output.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the 2026 FIFA World Cup five weeks away, a wave of injuries to key stars like Brazil's Rodrygo and Éder Militão (ACL tears), France's Hugo Ekitike (Achilles), Spain's Samu Aghehowa (ACL), and England's Jack Grealish (stress fracture) has leveled the field among top contenders, fueling the tight trader consensus atop France (16.4%) and Spain (15.3%). France edges ahead on recent friendly form, including a 2-1 win over Brazil behind Kylian Mbappé, and FIFA's No. 1 ranking, while Spain boasts Euro 2024 pedigree but faces a stern Group H test against Uruguay. England, Argentina, and Brazil trail closely due to squad depth offsetting aging cores like Lionel Messi and injury hits, underscoring the expanded 48-team format's knockout volatility.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the Washington Wizards win the 2026 NBA Finals. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve to “No” if it becomes impossible for this team to win the 2026 NBA Finals based off the rules of the NBA.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the NBA.

eventMetadata.context_description: Oklahoma City Thunder lead trader consensus at 57.5% implied probability to repeat as NBA champions after sweeping the Suns 4-0 in the first round and securing the easiest Western Conference path, facing the Lakers in the conference semifinals following L.A.'s 4-2 win over Houston. The Spurs follow at 21.4% after a 4-1 first-round victory over Portland, positioning Victor Wembanyama's squad against the Timberwolves, who upset Denver 4-2. Eastern Conference chaos—with Game 7s pending for Pistons-Magic, Celtics-76ers, and Cavaliers-Raptors—elevates the Knicks (7.7%) post their 4-2 series win over Atlanta, while contenders like Detroit (3.3%), Philadelphia (3.3%), and Cleveland (3.6%) remain viable amid upsets and no dominant force emerging. OKC's depth, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's MVP form, and playoff experience drive the heavy favoritism.

title: Eurovision Winner 2026
description:
This market will resolve to the country whose candidate for Eurovision 2026 wins.

If at any point it is impossible for the listed candidate to win Eurovision 2026 based on the rules of the competition (i.e. they are eliminated), this market may immediately resolve to "No".

If no winner is announced by July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve "Other". All ties will be broken according to EBU's official Eurovision rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Eurovision (https://eurovision.tv/), including live footage of Eurovision 2026, however a consensus of credible reporting will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: Vice President JD Vance commands trader consensus at 21% implied probability to win the 2028 presidential election, edging California Governor Gavin Newsom at 17.6%, with Marco Rubio third at 10.1%, reflecting GOP unity behind Trump's incumbent VP as heir apparent amid an open Democratic primary field post-Harris's 2024 defeat. Recent CPAC straw poll results from late March positioned Vance atop Republican nominee preferences, bolstered by his headlining of a major conservative donor summit and joint Iowa visits with Senator Ted Cruz signaling 2026 midterm and 2028 groundwork. Newsom maintains closeness via strong early California Democratic primary polling over Kamala Harris, but fragmented Dem contenders like AOC and Shapiro dilute support. The race stays tight over two years out, with 2026 midterms in swing states poised to test incumbency advantages and clarify paths to nomination amid uncertain national mood shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination at 26% implied probability, driven by his sustained national media presence, robust fundraising as California governor, and positioning as a sharp critic of the Trump administration amid ongoing policy clashes over immigration and climate. Recent signals from Kamala Harris, including her April statements at the National Action Network convention expressing interest in another White House bid and a South Carolina visit, have failed to close the gap, with her odds at 10% reflecting lingering electability concerns from 2024. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez trails at 8% on progressive grassroots appeal but faces broader electability hurdles, while Jon Ossoff's 6% surge ties to Georgia Senate incumbency advantages. The wide-open field could consolidate around frontrunners via 2026 midterm results elevating battleground governors like Josh Shapiro or Gretchen Whitmer, early primary polling in Iowa and New Hampshire, or decisive donor commitments before 2027 caucuses.

title: Elon Musk # tweets April 28 - May 5, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from April 28 12:00 PM ET to May 5, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

eventMetadata.context_description: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. commands 49% trader consensus as the 2028 Republican presidential nominee, narrowly ahead of Vice President J.D. Vance at 39%, propelled by RFK's high-visibility April testimonies defending vaccine guidance reforms, health spending cuts, and nutrition overhauls that resonate with populist voters via his Make America Healthy Again initiative. Vance's implied probability dipped amid mid-April polling declines tied to foreign policy scrutiny and Gen-Z hesitancy, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio lingers at 21% buoyed by a strong CPAC straw poll showing. This closely contested field underscores post-Trump succession uncertainty absent endorsements; 2026 midterms, fundraising tallies, Iowa caucuses groundwork, and official campaign launches could tip the balance toward a clearer frontrunner.

title: F1 Drivers' Champion
description:
This market will resolve according to the listed driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2026 F1 season.

This market will resolve as soon as the official results of the final scheduled race of the 2026 F1 season are known.

If multiple drivers tie for first place in the drivers standings, this market will resolve according to the tiebreak procedure used by F1 to determine the 2026 F1 Drivers’ champion.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2026 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), the corresponding market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

eventMetadata.context_description: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli holds a narrow seven-point lead in the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship standings at 75 points over teammate George Russell's 68 following yesterday's Miami Grand Prix Sprint, where a five-second track limits penalty dropped the rookie from a potential podium to sixth, elevating Russell to fourth and preserving the tight intra-team battle. Antonelli's back-to-back victories in China and Japan—his maiden F1 win in Shanghai—have fueled trader consensus at 34.4% implied probability, while Russell's podium consistency, including the Australian GP win, sustains his 29.0% at 29.0%, underscoring Mercedes' dominant car amid Red Bull's Max Verstappen struggles further back at 9.5%. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc trails third at 55 points, keeping the top fight fiercely contested with 17 races remaining.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 5 - May 12, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from May 5 12:00 PM ET to May 12, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.

Recent quiet spells through May 2 gave way to bursts exceeding 10 posts on viral demographics debates (e.g., Italy's birth collapse), political flashpoints like deportations and school protests, plus Starlink's Papua New Guinea rollout and Grok Voice benchmarks. This volatility creates uncertainty: sustained restraint could favor lower bins, while engagement spikes on culture-war topics or company updates (Tesla earnings proximity) might push toward 200+. Watch daily momentum as real-time cultural force shapes outcomes.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket prices Jordan Bardella at 22.5% and Édouard Philippe at 21.5% to win the 2027 French presidential election, reflecting a fragmented field where no candidate dominates amid post-municipal election shifts in March 2026. Bardella leads first-round polls at 34-42% (Harris, Verian April), buoyed by National Rally's anti-incumbent appeal following years of unstable governments under Prime Ministers Barnier, Bayrou, and Lecornu, plus Marine Le Pen's pending ineligibility appeal on July 7. Philippe, Horizons leader, gained from his strong Le Havre mayoral reelection, polling competitively at 18-36% first round and edging Bardella in some runoffs (Elabe 51.5-48.5%). Left fragmentation and a United Left primary in October could consolidate opposition, while Les Républicains' Retailleau selection adds center-right competition; economic pressures or scandals may tip the balance before April 2027 voting.

Holmes' command could exploit Angels' shaky bullpen.

Partial loss of territory or challenges from rebel or exile groups will not qualify unless the Islamic Republic no longer administers the majority of the Iranian population within Iran. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

description: What will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit in May 2026?

markets.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $150 in May?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation during May 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "Low" price equal to or above the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during the applicable trading session for the underlying market will be considered. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours. 

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract’s last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract’s last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date.

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "Low" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader sentiment for WTI crude oil price levels in May 2026 hinges on persistent Strait of Hormuz disruptions from Middle East military actions since late February, which spiked front-month futures to over $110/bbl in Q1 before a recent pullback to around $102/bbl as of May 1. The latest EIA data for the week ended April 24 revealed a 6.2 million barrel inventory drawdown to 459.5 million barrels, bolstering prices amid robust U.S. exports, though softening global demand from China weighs on outlooks. OPEC+ approved a 206,000 bpd quota increase for May contingent on Hormuz reopening, compounded by UAE's impending exit from the group, heightening supply risks. Key catalysts include the May 6 EIA report and potential geopolitical de-escalations influencing month-end settlements.

title: US x Iran permanent peace deal by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran and the United states agree to a permanent peace deal by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

A permanent peace deal refers to any agreement which explicitly indicates that military hostilities between the United States and Iran have ended or will permanently cease, or uses equivalent language clearly signaling a lasting end to military hostilities between the United States and Iran. Agreements that are explicitly temporary or which do not include a definitive agreement to end military hostilities between the US and Iran on a lasting basis (e.g. a temporary extension of the two-week ceasefire agreement announced on April 7, 2026), will not qualify.

A qualifying agreement will be considered to have been established if either of the following conditions are met:

- The United States and Iran each sign or formally adopt a written agreement (e.g. a treaty or multi-point agreement) which meets the above criteria.

- Both the governments of the United States and Iran provide clear public confirmation that a qualifying agreement has been definitively established. Negotiations, statements of progress, or other statements which do not constitute a definitive announcement that a qualifying agreement has been reached will not count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Amid a fragile ceasefire extension following the 2026 US-Iran war, indirect negotiations mediated by Pakistan and Oman have stalled after Iran submitted a revised 14-point proposal on May 1, which President Trump rejected for lacking nuclear concessions and guarantees on uranium enrichment limits. Key sticking points include reopening the Strait of Hormuz without Iranian fees, lifting sanctions, US troop withdrawals from the region, and verifiable curbs on Tehran's nuclear program—echoing past JCPOA disputes. Trump has vowed to maintain the naval blockade until a comprehensive deal emerges, while Iranian officials warn of ceasefire collapse without progress. Traders watch for upcoming White House reviews and potential mediator breakthroughs, as military escalation risks remain high despite diplomatic channels staying open.

title: US x Iran diplomatic meeting by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding US-Iranian relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count. 

The meeting must be in-person and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran, and a consensus of credible reporting.

This follows a failed marathon session and planned but unconfirmed in-person talks in Islamabad last month involving US envoys like JD Vance, Jared Kushner, and Steve Witkoff, and Iranian officials including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. No direct diplomatic meeting has materialized recently, with exchanges remaining indirect amid disputes over nuclear limits and sanctions relief. Traders monitor Trump's upcoming national security meeting and potential escalation signals, as historical patterns show such impasses often prolong tensions before breakthroughs.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Eastern Conference first-round series between the Cleveland Cavaliers and Toronto Raptors is tied 3-3 heading into Game 7 today at Rocket Arena, where home-court advantage has proven decisive as the home team won all six prior contests. Raptors' momentum stems from their 112-110 overtime victory in Game 6 on May 1, fueled by RJ Barrett's buzzer-beating 3-pointer and strong play from Scottie Barnes, but they face challenges without Immanuel Quickley (hamstring, out for playoffs) and with Brandon Ingram questionable (right heel inflammation). Cavaliers, healthier aside from Thomas Bryant (calf, out), rely on Donovan Mitchell and James Harden to capitalize on the do-or-die home matchup against a resilient Raptors squad showing playoff grit.

On April 12, 2026, President Donald Trump announced that the United States will blockade the Strait of Hormuz. You can read more about that here: https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/live-blog/live-updates-us-iran-fail-reach-deal-peace-talks-day-negotiations-rcna315918.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if President Trump, the US government, or the US military publicly and officially announces the end of the United States blockade of the Strait of Hormuz by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Qualifying statements must clearly and explicitly indicate that the United States has lifted, ended, or will lift or end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz on a specified date or use equivalently definitive language unambiguously signaling that such blockade has ceased or is set to cease on a specified date (e.g., statements unambiguously indicating that US naval activity in the relevant area has ceased will qualify). 

Statements that merely describe actions inconsistent with the blockade (e.g., "Iran resumed shipping through the Strait of Hormuz") without explicitly indicating the blockade as lifted will not alone suffice.

Informal announcements, statements from unnamed sources, or leaks do not qualify.

Written public statements from Donald Trump (e.g., posts from his personal Truth Social account) will qualify. Videos posted on his social media accounts will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the US government and/or its official representatives; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

Note: this market will resolve solely based on whether a qualifying announcement is made within the specified timeframe. Whether the blockade is effectively enforced or whether maritime traffic resumes absent a qualifying announcement will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: President Trump's rejection of Iran's latest proposal yesterday keeps the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in place, conditioning its lift on a comprehensive nuclear deal amid ongoing economic warfare. Imposed April 12 after US-Iran talks collapsed, the blockade enforces sanctions on Iranian ports despite Tehran removing its own restrictions days later; recent US actions include ship interceptions, warnings to shipping firms against Iranian tolls, and calls for allied support to reopen the waterway. With crude prices surging, trader consensus reflects prolonged pressure until diplomatic concessions, though no new talks or summits are scheduled. Escalation risks persist if Iran retaliates or global energy disruptions mount.

title: Brazil Presidential Election
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent polls from AtlasIntel/Bloomberg (April 28) and BTG Pactual/Nexus show Senator Flávio Bolsonaro holding a slim first-round edge over President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with statistical ties in simulated runoffs, driving trader consensus to price Flávio at 43.5% and Lula at 38.5% for the October 4 election winner. This tight race reflects Brazil's deep political polarization, Lula's incumbency advantage offset by stagnating approval ratings amid economic pressures like inflation and fiscal deficits, and Flávio's consolidation of right-wing support via the enduring Bolsonaro family brand despite his father's ineligibility. Fragmented opposition—Renan Santos, Camilo Santana, and governors like Romeu Zema trailing—raises second-round likelihood on October 25. Separation could stem from party conventions by August, economic data releases, or scandals swaying undecided voters in swing regions like the Northeast and Southeast.

eventMetadata.context_description: With the Eastern Conference first-round series tied 3-3, Detroit Pistons host Orlando Magic in a winner-take-all Game 7 at Little Caesars Arena, where the top-seeded Pistons (60-22 regular season) hold home-court advantage and momentum from their 93-79 Game 6 rout behind Cade Cunningham's fourth-quarter dominance. Orlando, the No. 8 seed, faces major setbacks with Franz Wagner ruled out for a third straight game (right calf strain) and Jonathan Isaac doubtful (left knee sprain), thinning their wing depth and forcing heavier reliance on Paolo Banchero amid a 1-2 skid. Detroit cleared Tobias Harris (left ankle) to play Game 6 but lists Kevin Huerter as questionable (left adductor), bolstering their trader-favored edge in this high-stakes elimination matchup.

eventMetadata.context_description: Tom Steyer holds a narrow lead in trader consensus for California's June 2 top-two primary at 42.8% implied probability, buoyed by his $132 million self-funding blitz dominating airwaves, while Xavier Becerra trails closely at 34.3% after surging in post-debate polls to 24% in some surveys like Gudelunas (April 23-27), capitalizing on Eric Swalwell's early exit and strong debate performances. The race stays tight due to high undecideds (23% in Emerson April polling), fragmented Democratic support among Katie Porter and Matt Mahan, and Republican vote-splitting between Steve Hilton and Chad Bianco, risking a Dem-only runoff in the blue state. Ballots mailing soon, late endorsements or turnout surges could tip frontrunners.

title: US obtains Iranian enriched uranium by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the US government or military officially announces or confirms that it has gained possession of any quantity of enriched uranium previously controlled by Iran by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

“Possession” means that the United States has actual physical custody or control of the enriched uranium, whether held within U.S. territory or elsewhere. Announcements of deals, agreements, commitments, or plans under which the United States would acquire possession of Iranian enriched uranium at a later time will not qualify.

Qualifying possession of Iranian enriched uranium may be acquired through any means, including through an agreed surrender or seizure.

A widespread consensus of credible reporting that the United States has gained possession of Iranian enriched uranium will also qualify for a “Yes” resolution, even if the United States makes no formal announcement.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States; however, a widespread consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus reflects deep skepticism on near-term US acquisition of Iranian enriched uranium, with implied probabilities around 9-10% by May 31 amid stalled post-ceasefire diplomacy. Iran's Atomic Energy Organization chief recently affirmed protecting enrichment rights as essential for talks, while Tehran deems its 60% enriched stockpile—estimated at over 400 kg pre-strikes—"sacred" and non-transferable. Trump dismissed Iran's Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal that deferred nuclear issues, and leaked intelligence questions the efficacy of prior US-Israeli airstrikes in eliminating facilities like Isfahan. IAEA-Russia-US extraction discussions continue without breakthroughs, leaving diplomatic impasse and Iran's assertions as key barriers, though year-end odds near 28% account for potential escalation or concessions before December 31.

title: Fed Decision in June?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's June 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their June meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Polymarket traders price a 95.5% implied probability for no change in the federal funds rate at the June 17-18, 2026 FOMC meeting, reflecting the Fed's April 29 hold at 3.50%-3.75% amid resilient economic data. Chair Powell's press conference signaled caution, citing March nonfarm payroll gains of 178,000 jobs, unemployment steady at 4.3%, and core CPI easing to 2.6% year-over-year but remaining above target. Major banks including J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, and Wells Fargo have shifted forecasts to steady policy through 2026, eroding prior cut expectations. This strong consensus could face pressure from softer May jobs or CPI prints, though recent trends suggest limited near-term catalysts for deviation.
